question: How should the Canaanites be treated?
summary: The Pentateuch and Joshua give four incompatible answers about what Israel was to do with the Canaanites. God promises to drive them out himself via hornets and an angel (Exodus 23, 33-34; Josh 3, 13, 23). Deuteronomy 7 and 20 command total extermination with no survivors. Numbers 33 says drive them out and destroy their cult sites. Ezekiel 47 envisions resident aliens inheriting land alongside Israel. These are not complementary policies — they are different programs.

reconcile.connective: Defenders collapse the drive-out and exterminate commands into one program, reading "drive out" not as expulsion but as the very extermination Deuteronomy 7 prescribes.

discrepancy.connective: Steven DiMattei presses the row directly, arguing the dispossession texts (Exodus 23; Numbers 33) and Deuteronomy's herem of utter annihilation come from different documentary sources and "cannot be harmonized."

skeptic.name: Steven DiMattei
skeptic.work: Contradictions in the Bible, "Were the Israelites to dispossess the indigenous Canaanites OR utterly destroy them?" (contradictionsinthebible.com/dispossess-or-destroy)
skeptic.attribution: Steven DiMattei, Contradictions in the Bible (online), "Dispossess or Destroy?"

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on Exodus 23:20-33
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D treat this passage directly, reconciling the 'hornet'/drive-out promise with the extermination command by reading expulsion and destruction as conditional, progressive stages of one conquest ('not drive them away at once ... He would drive them out by degrees'), and noting Israel's failure to exterminate is what left Canaanites in the land.

link.note: No allowlisted page squarely harmonizes THIS pair (drive-out/dispossess vs. exterminate). gotquestions.org/Canaanites-extermination.html defends the morality of the herem but does not reconcile the drive-out language with it; defendinginerrancy.com Deuteronomy_20.16-18_(2).php addresses the same passage but a different mechanism (spare far-off cities vs. destroy Canaanite cities), not the dispossess-vs-annihilate axis. excerpts.on_tension_rationale: The single sharpest harmonizing sentence on the row: JFB explicitly reads Numbers' 'drive out' as NOT expulsion but the extermination of Deut 7:1, collapsing the dispossess vs. annihilate axis into one command. excerpts.source_note_text:
ye shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you--not, however, by expulsion, but extermination (Deu 7:1).
and destroy all their pictures--obelisks for idolatrous worship (see on Lev 26:1).
and destroy all their molten images, and quite pluck down all their high places--by metonymy for all their groves and altars, and materials of worship on the tops of hills.
